title: Enterprise isolation adoption roadmap: cohort-based migration playbook and OKR alignment
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Objective: produce a cohort-based playbook that standardizes how we onboard mid-to-large enterprise customers into Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments for Q2 launches. The playbook will map technical runbooks, GTM artifacts, metric targets (OKRs), pricing delta guidance, and cross-functional roles so Sales, Solutions, Eng, and Support can execute predictable migrations.

Scope:
- Create 3 migration cohorts (Pilot <5 seats, Scale 5-50 seats, Island >50 seats) with tailored acceptance criteria and SLAs.
- Define onboarding runbooks: network checklist (VPC peering, routes), SSO/SAML mapping, KMS/HSM key handoff procedure, data residency checklist, and ops playbook for upgrades.
- OKR alignment: measurable targets for adoption rate, time-to-onboard, post-onboard reliability metrics, and revenue milestones.
- GTM assets: customer-facing migration timeline template, pricing worksheet, and partner enablement kit.
- Integrations with Console: onboarding dashboard signals and telemetry for cohort progression.

Out of scope: deep rewrites of RBAC engine (targeted for Q3) and extended on-prem installer rearchitecture.

Success criteria: cohort onboarding material published, two pilot customers migrated using the playbook, and tracking dashboards live in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Three cohort definitions documented with clear sizing and acceptance gates
Onboarding runbooks published to Confluence with checklist items and owner assignments
Two pilot migrations completed and retro documented
Console onboarding dashboard captures cohort status and time-to-onboard metric
OKR targets agreed and added to the Private Deployments initiative
risks: Dependency on ENG-45231 (networking templates); delays there extend onboarding pilots
Security review may require changes to KMS handoff which could shift go-live
Sales enablement uptake lower than expected if pricing guidance is unclear
Console telemetry requires a lightweight schema addition which could conflict with existing dashboards
